title: Ohio LLC for Non-Residents: Cost and Steps (2026)
h1: How to Form an Ohio LLC as a Non-Resident (2026 Cost and Steps)
description: How non-US founders form an Ohio LLC in 2026: $99 articles of organization, no annual report, an Ohio statutory agent, EIN, Form 5472 and address tips.
llms_summary: A non-resident can form an Ohio LLC for a $99 state fee, must keep an Ohio statutory agent with a street address in the state, and does not file an annual report with the Secretary of State.
body_html:
Short answer: Anyone can form an Ohio LLC from abroad, with no US citizenship, residency or visa. You file articles of organization with the Ohio Secretary of State for $99, appoint a statutory agent with an Ohio street address who signs a written acceptance, then get an EIN from the IRS. Ohio's fee statute lists no annual or biennial report for LLCs, so there is no yearly state report fee. The one ongoing state rule is that you must keep a statutory agent at all times.

What Ohio charges

Ohio sets its filing fees in Revised Code section 111.16.

  • Articles of organization: $99, paid once.
  • Annual report: none. The statute and the state's published fee list include no LLC annual or biennial report.
  • Change of statutory agent or agent address: $25.
  • Amendment or correction to the articles: $50.
  • Certificate of dissolution or cancellation: $50.
  • Reinstatement after cancellation: $25.
  • Registering an LLC formed in another state: $99.
  • EIN: free from the IRS.

Commercial statutory agent fees are extra and set by each provider. Ohio also offers paid expedited filing, so check the Secretary of State's fee schedule for current options before you file.

Step by step

  1. Check the name in the Ohio Secretary of State business search.
  2. Choose a statutory agent. It must be an Ohio resident or a business entity with a business address in Ohio.
  3. File the articles of organization. By law they must give the LLC's name and the statutory agent's name and street address, with the agent's signed written acceptance. The state will not accept articles without that acceptance.
  4. Sign an operating agreement. It is kept by the company, not filed, and banks often ask for it.
  5. Get an EIN with Form SS-4, then open a bank account.

The statutory agent rule

Ohio calls the registered agent a statutory agent, and section 1706.09 of the Revised Code sets strict rules:

  • A company agent must use its usual place of business in Ohio, which must be open during normal business hours with someone present to accept legal papers. A post office box does not qualify, even one with a street address.
  • If the agent resigns, its authority ends 30 days after it files the resignation, and you must appoint a new agent straight away.
  • If the LLC fails to keep an agent, the Secretary of State sends a notice. Unless the problem is fixed within 30 days, the articles are canceled without further action. A canceled LLC can apply for reinstatement within two years.

For a founder abroad, this is the main way an Ohio LLC is lost: the agent service lapses, the notice goes unread and the company is canceled. Keep the agent paid and your contact details current.

Privacy: what is public

Ohio's articles of organization only have to show the LLC's name and the statutory agent's details. Member and manager names are not required, although you may add them. With no annual report, there is also no yearly filing that lists owners. That makes Ohio more private than states such as Montana, where member or manager names appear in public filings.

Federal steps for non-resident owners

These apply to every US LLC, whatever the state.

  • EIN: without an SSN or ITIN you apply with Form SS-4 by fax or mail. See how to get an EIN without an SSN.
  • Form 5472: a single-member LLC owned by a non-US person files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 each year, due April 15, even with no income. See Form 5472 for foreign-owned LLCs.
  • BOI: LLCs formed in the US, including Ohio LLCs, are exempt from FinCEN beneficial ownership reporting under the final rule effective August 14, 2026. See BOI reporting in 2026.

Ohio taxes to keep in mind

An Ohio LLC does not pay a state annual report fee, but Ohio does have taxes that can apply to business activity in the state, including the commercial activity tax on gross receipts and municipal income taxes in many cities. Whether any of them apply depends on where your sales and work actually happen. Check the Ohio Department of Taxation's current guidance or ask an Ohio tax adviser before you rely on Ohio being tax free.

Statutory agent address vs business address

The statutory agent address is where the state and courts send legal notices. It is not automatically your business or mailing address, and many agents do not forward everyday mail or let you use their address for banking.

Banks and payment providers usually ask for a business address and for each owner's real personal residential address, which for most non-residents is their home abroad. Many banks decline CMRA or virtual mailbox addresses as a business address, so check the bank's eligibility page before you apply. See what a CMRA address is.

Ohio vs Wyoming or Delaware

Ohio's $99 formation fee is higher than some states, but with no annual report the long-run state cost is low, and owner names stay off the articles. It fits best if you have customers, staff or a warehouse in Ohio. For a remote online business with no Ohio connection, compare Wyoming and Wyoming vs Delaware first.

The Residential Address forms Ohio LLCs for non-US founders, including the EIN application. See LLC formation.

This article is general information, not tax or legal advice.
faqs: Can a non-US citizen form an Ohio LLC?
Yes. Ohio has no citizenship or residency requirement for LLC owners. You need a statutory agent who is an Ohio resident or a business with an Ohio business address.
How much does an Ohio LLC cost to form?
The articles of organization cost $99 under Ohio Revised Code section 111.16. Statutory agent fees are extra.
Does an Ohio LLC file an annual report?
No. Ohio's fee statute lists no annual or biennial report for LLCs. You must, however, keep a statutory agent at all times.
What happens if my Ohio LLC loses its statutory agent?
The Secretary of State sends a notice, and if no new agent is appointed within 30 days the articles are canceled. The LLC can apply for reinstatement within two years for a $25 fee.
Are owner names public for an Ohio LLC?
Not by default. The articles only require the LLC's name and the statutory agent's name, street address and signed acceptance.
